Barreleye Fish: Those Aren't Its Eyes 😱
seo_intro:
What are the two dots on the barreleye fish's face? Fake eyes, nostrils, or glowing lights?
The barreleye fish (Macropinna microstoma) has a see-through head: the dots are its nostrils, and its real eyes are the glowing green domes inside its transparent head, which can rotate to look up.
sources: Robison, B. H. & Reisenbichler, K. R. (2008). Macropinna microstoma and the Paradox of Its Tubular Eyes. Copeia 2008(4): 780–784 (MBARI)
Live Science — Barreleye fish: the deep-sea weirdo with rotating eyes and a see-through head

tiktok_text:
Two thousand feet deep lives a fish with a see-through head 🐟 And those two dots on its face aren't its eyes. Fake eyes, nostrils, or glowing lights? They're nostrils! This is the barreleye fish: its real eyes are the two green domes inside its transparent head, and they can rotate to look straight up through its own head at prey above. Nets used to crush that fragile head, so it was only filmed alive in the 2000s.
